study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Coupé et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2022
study_identification_part.si4_title: Hippocampal-amygdalo-ventricular atrophy score: Alzheimer disease detection using normative and pathological lifespan models

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Propose HAVAs, a simple MRI-based score combining normative (CN) and pathological (AD) lifespan volume models to detect AD and predict MCI progression, and compare performance against normative modeling, classical ML, and DL with external validation.

caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: "we proposed new scores of being an AD patient (respectively a CN subject) based on the distance to the models ..."; "we used 2 σ as threshold to detect abnormal values when using normative model-based methods"

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Diagnostic classification metrics (BACC, SPE, SEN, AUC) for AD vs CN and prognosis (pMCI vs sMCI); comparisons to normative modeling, DL (ClinicaDL), and classical ML (SVM, LASSO) baselines.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: HAVAs achieved high AD vs CN accuracy on external datasets (AUC ≥ 94%) and discriminated pMCI vs sMCI (AUC ≈ 78%), outperforming normative, ML, and DL baselines.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Across AIBL and MIRIAD external datasets, HAVAs showed very accurate AD detection (AUC ≥ 94%) and, on ADNI, achieved AUC ~78% for pMCI vs sMCI classification. Screening identified hippocampus, amygdala, and inferior lateral ventricle as most discriminant, and combining them into HAVAs improved performance over single-ROI normative, deep learning (ClinicaDL ROI/subject/patch CNNs), and classical ML (SVM/LASSO) approaches.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: HAVAs intended for clinical use due to simplicity and interpretability; authors state HAVAs will be made available on volBrain/AssemblyNet-AD.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: HC mean age (36.07 years) computed as weighted mean across CN datasets in Table 1; SD not reported. No explicit site harmonization (e.g., ComBat/HBR) described beyond ICV normalization and z-scoring. MCI groups defined using ClinicaDL selection criteria; pMCI converts within 36 months; sMCI stable over 3 years.
